newsitem.title: USA: Black leaders convene to warn of AIDS crisis.
newsitem.headline: Black leaders convene to warn of AIDS crisis.

text.p: A group of black community leaders on Tuesday urged the White House to hold an emergency meeting to address the disproportionate toll AIDS is taking on black Americans.
Attendees at the "Leading for Life Summit" heard that AIDS kills twice as many black men between the ages of 25 and 44 as homicide and that two-thirds of all women with AIDS are black.

"We appeal to our national government to convene an emergency meeting of the appropriate cabinet-level officials to address AIDS within groups of colour," said Henry Louis Gates Jr., director of Harvard's African-American studies department.
"Specifically that appeal is addressed to the president of the United States, no matter who might win (the election) in two weeks," he told reporters at a press conference.
The conference attendees, including Children's Defence Fund founder Marian Wright Edelman, said the summit was a first step in raising awareness of AIDS in the black community.
"We came together not just to talk about AIDS but to plan a strategy to act on AIDS," Edelman said. "Obviously I will be making extra effort to advocate for sick children from this killer disease."
She said that that black children account for more than half of pedriatric AIDS cases.

Also at the conference, held at Harvard University, was Patsy Fleming, the top AIDS adviser to President Bill Cliinton, David Satcher, director of the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention and others from business, academia and the entertainment, media and political communities.
But some attendees said they were troubled that other prominent black Americans chose to skip the conference.

"This meeting is to send them a clear signal that they better start standing firm because we are going to hold them accountable for their absence and their silence. Let's be clear about that," said Mario Cooper, a member of the Harvard AIDS Institute.

The Harvard AIDS Institute plans to hold another conference on the impact of AIDS on the Latin-American community in the next year or two, said Alvin Poussaint, a professor of psychiatry at the Harvard Medical School.
